patches.value: image of a e_i in M_R/pM_R and its scalar extension to M tensor_Z K
For each 0<=i<=lambda, define b_i as the image of a e_i under M_R -> M_R/pM_R and then under the canonical identification (M_R/pM_R) tensor_F_p K = M tensor_Z K.
Let W be any K-subspace invariant under x,y,h.

On the R-basis a e_0,...,a e_lambda established above, x(ae_i)=(lambda-i+1)ae_(i-1), y(ae_i)=(i+1)ae_(i+1), and h(ae_i)=(lambda-2i)ae_i, with out-of-range terms zero. Let F_p be the prime subfield of K, canonically isomorphic to R/pR=Z/pZ. The images of a e_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R because they are an R-basis of M_R. The natural map M_R/pM_R -> M tensor_Z F_p is an isomorphism: for a Z-basis of M, localization at integers prime to p reduces to the same F_p-basis. Extending scalars F_p -> K gives the K-basis b_0,...,b_lambda of M tensor_Z K, where b_i denotes the image of a e_i under these quotient and scalar-extension maps. These maps carry each integral action matrix to its reduction and then to K, so x b_i=(lambda-i+1)b_(i-1), y b_i=(i+1)b_(i+1), h b_i=(lambda-2i)b_i, with out-of-range terms zero. Thus this explicitly identifies the reduced representation and action; the characteristic-zero e_i are not vectors of M tensor_Z K.

For 0<=r<=lambda<p, r! is invertible modulo p, so the reductions of X_r and Y_r are scalar multiples of the corresponding powers of x and y on M tensor_Z K. The characteristic-zero identities defining E_i,j preserve M_R and their matrices in the R-basis a e_t are the usual matrix-unit matrices. Reduction modulo p and extension to K therefore give the matrix units in the explicitly defined basis b_0,...,b_lambda; equivalently the identities from S002 persist under these maps. Every binom(lambda,j) is nonzero modulo p because 0<=j<=lambda<p, hence is a unit in F_p and K. Thus any K-subspace W invariant under x and y is invariant under each reduced E_i,j. Write a nonzero w in W as w=sum_i c_i b_i and choose i with c_i nonzero. For every j, the reduced E_j,i sends w to c_i b_j, so b_j belongs to W because c_i is invertible in K. Hence W is the whole module. The basis has lambda+1 vectors, a positive integer, so the module is nonzero. This proves irreducibility, including lambda=0 and p=2.
